newsitem.title: USA: Cell Genesys, Somatix to merge.
newsitem.headline: Cell Genesys, Somatix to merge.

text.p: Gene therapy companies Cell Genesys Inc and Somatix Therapy Corp said Monday they agreed to merge in a stock-for-stock deal.
Under the terms of the deal, which was unanimously approved by the boards of both companies, Somatix would become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Cell Genesys.
Somatix stockholders would receive 0.385 share of Cell Genesys stock for each share of Somatix stock, subject to adjustment in certain circumstances.
Cell Genesys stockholders would own about 61 percent of the combined company.
The companies expect to lay off about 20 percent of the total workforce, due to the closing of Somatix's Alameda site and the consolidation of research and development programs.
The companies were not immediately available to comment on the size of the current workforce.

The majority of the transaction price is expected to be characterized as "in-process research and development," which would involve a one-time charge during the quarter in which stockholders approved the merger.
The deal is expected to be completed in April, the companies said.

Cell Genesys and Somatix said they expect to reduce overall projected net cash expenditures and maintain current financial strength. Excluding one-time merger-related expenses, the companies expect the net burn rate of the combined entity would be about $20 million in 1997.
Stephen Sherwin, Cell Genesis' chairman and chief executive, would be president and chief executive officer of the combined company, the companies said.
David Carter, who is currently chairman and chief executive officer of Somatix, would be elected to the new board of directors, the companies said.

"A new configuration of Somatix's GVAX cancer vaccine will begin clinical trials in lung cancer this year, with the goal of identifying a more attractive economic profile for this product candidate," Sherwin said.

"While we will continue to evaluate efficacy data from recently completed clinical trials of the current GVAX product configuration, we do not plan to initiate new trials including a potential Phase III trial for melanoma," Sherwin said.
The companies plan to combine the Cell Genesys and Somatix stem cell programs into a broader research effort and focus on medical needs including AIDS and cancer.
Over the course of the next three months, the companies will evaluate partnering opportunities for these programs and finalize the research and development strategy.
